advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where a configured analyzer's analyze() returns Unavailable and assert analyze_or_unavailable passes that Unavailable through unchanged.
evidence: Analyzer Protocol return type is `AnalyzerResult | Unavailable` (src/rebar/metrics/analyzer.py:28)
Pass-through of the analyzer result is unconditional: `return analyzer.analyze(repo_root, languages=languages)` (src/rebar/metrics/analyzer.py:55)
test_analyzer.py only configures `_RecordingAnalyzer` returning an `AnalyzerResult` (test_analyzer.py:34-36); the Unavailable-from-configured-analyzer branch is exercised by neither test file
ABSENCE: heldout test covers ONLY the `analyzer is None` Unavailable branch (test_analyzer_heldout.py:25-37), not a configured analyzer returning Unavailable
advisory.finding: No test exercises a CONFIGURED analyzer whose analyze() returns Unavailable; analyze_or_unavailable forwards that value verbatim (analyzer.py:55), so a regression that wrapped/swallowed a configured analyzer's own Unavailable would pass all current tests.
scenarios: A configured adapter reports Unavailable (e.g. missing toolchain) — downstream must receive that Unavailable unchanged
A future refactor wraps/normalizes the analyzer return value and accidentally coerces or drops its Unavailable
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that registers an analyzer returning `Unavailable(reason=..., accruing_since=...)` and asserts `analyze_or_unavailable(...) is/== that Unavailable` (i.e. the configured analyzer's own Unavailable is forwarded verbatim, not the 'no analyzer configured' reason).
